note: S0673's formalization of a fact as F=(p,v): proposition plus graded epistemic assessment, distinguishing p from E_t(p) (epistemic evaluation) from P_t(p) (probabilistic representation), with a layered Observations->Evidence->Fact->Logic->Epistemic Assessment->Knowledge State pipeline. Distinct from typed-mathematical-epistemic-model (B0012, Knowledge Vector K) and knowledge-measure-theory-v0-1 (B0014, measure over Knowledge Space) though thematically continuous with the phase_measure_theory brainstorming thread.

aliases: Knowledge Modelling & KnowledgeOS Kernel -- Knowledge Transfer for New Session
note: S0675/S0676's session-transfer synthesis document: converges the phase_measure_theory research thread into a candidate Core (P,T,B,I,E,K,R,H,Theta), a DDD bounded-context map, a Zero Lens admission test, Roberts measurement governance, Shani invariants, a Core Admission Matrix, and explicit corrections/prohibitions; declares itself a synthesis artifact, not primary authority. Its Core tuple closely parallels but is not identical to relational-structure-core-regime-model's Kfrak=(P,C,T,X,I,E,R,Lambda) (B0014) -- flagged as possibly the same evolving object, not confirmed.

aliases: The Conditional Evidence Problem research synthesis
note: S0677's systematic comparison of eight conditional-evidence-combination formalisms (Bayesian probability, Dempster-Shafer, fuzzy/many-valued logic, non-monotonic logic, argumentation theory, epistemic logic, temporal logic, measurement theory) against Knowledge Space Theory's (KST) response-function/Bayesian-update/assessment-update model, asking what invariant (if any) survives across mechanisms when applied to the same substrate; proposes the Kernel-preserves-raw-evidence / Regime-determines-combination-mechanism architecture. Distinct from but engaging the same KST (Q,K) reference as meta-epistemic-kernel-substrate-hypothesis (B0015) -- flagged possibly related, not confirmed identical object.

notations: p <- R <- E <- O (with C,t,M attached)
note: S0678's proposed deeper Kernel invariant candidate: instead of 'the set of possible states consistent with evidence' (S0677's hypothesis, here challenged as regime-dependent and untested), the more fundamental invariant may be the determination lineage -- why p was determined, reconstructible as p<-R<-E<-O with context/time/method attached -- termed 'epistemic provenance'; reframes the research question as two-dimensional (Question A: what epistemic structure is invariant across evidence-combination regimes; Question B: what substrate must be preserved so regimes can reconstruct their determinations) and poses 'What is the minimum substrate required to reconstruct a conditional determination?' as the hardest unresolved question.

aliases: Determination is the missing mathematical object
note: S0679's critique of an uploaded framework document (Observation->Evidence->Fact->Comparison->Rule/Logic->Justification->Knowledge, with P(F|I) and (F_{<=t},S_t,R_t)->K_t): argues the framework's listed 'invariants' are not proven invariants but merely dimensions along which frameworks differ, that a common algebraic structure is premature, that epistemic state may be multidimensional (proposition/support/justification/status/uncertainty/time), and that Determination D_t(p) -- the operation (O,E,F_{<t},C,R)->D_t(p) -- is the missing explicit mathematical object needed before invariance can responsibly be discussed. Related to but distinct from determination-lineage-invariant (S0678, which emphasizes provenance/reconstruction of why p was determined) -- this document emphasizes Determination as a first-class formal object/operation in its own right. Per the git history, this brainstorming later becomes formalized as MD-104's 'Determination is the missing mathematical object' framing.

S0680's major synthesis proposing an abstract epistemic state S (not identified with any single regime's representation) updated by a regime-specific operator U_R, queried via Answer_R/Explain_R/Measure_R, with a candidate invariant I(S) = (Content,Participant,Context,Time,Commitment,Support,Incompatibility,Consequence,Provenance,Transition) that must be preserved by any semantics-preserving mapping phi between two regimes' representations for them to be 'task-equivalent'; names this candidate (not-yet-proved) result 'Epistemic Representation Invariance' and the underlying question 'Epistemic State Equivalence'. Per the git history this becomes a named candidate theorem in MD-104. Distinct from but builds directly on conditional-evidence-combination-landscape (S0677) and determination-as-mathematical-object (S0679).

aliases: The Kernel Problem: Minimum Substrate for Conditional Determination
note: S0680's formal treatment of 'what is the minimum substrate required to reconstruct a conditional determination under multiple regimes': shifts from Knowledge-as-storage to Substrate-for-reconstruction, analyzes KST's own substrate (Q,K,O,r,p,u), derives per-regime substrate requirements for Bayesian/Dempster-Shafer/non-monotonic/argumentation, and proposes the KnowledgeOS Kernel Hypothesis S_Kernel=(D,E,S,T,U) (domain, evidence, sources, temporal structure, uncertainty metadata) as the minimum common substrate -- explicitly a research hypothesis, not an established fact. Possibly the same evolving idea as determination-lineage-invariant's 'minimum substrate for conditional determination' framing (S0678) -- flagged, not confirmed identical.

notations: IDEAL STATE -> OBSERVATION -> EXTRACTION -> COMPARISON -> DETERMINATION -> FACT -> KNOWLEDGE
note: S0685's reframing of the whole pipeline: humans first hold/conceive an Ideal State I_t (the complete state of what is supposed to be known/true/valid), and Knowledge/Facts are produced by comparing observations against that ideal via reasoning, not by building an ideal state up from raw observations. Distinguishes the theoretical ideal I_t from our estimated hat I_t (hat I_t != I_t in general), reframes Knowledge as identified elements/relationships of the ideal state (K_t subset-or-approx I_t), places probability at the extraction of hat I_t from imperfect observations and logic at the ideal<->observed comparison, and raises 'where does the Ideal State come from?' (reality / human model / normative model / domain model / mathematical ideal / combination) as the most important unresolved problem, ahead of any Kernel definition.

S0691's distinction within the ideal-state-comparison-model between two fundamentally different uncertainties: (1) known dimension, unknown value (ordinary uncertainty, e.g. certificate expiry date unknown) and (2) unknown dimension (uncertainty about whether an additional relevant dimension of the ideal state exists at all, e.g. an undiscovered dependency) -- the latter being uncertainty about the structure of the knowledge space itself, not about a value within it. Splits knowledge-completeness into dimension coverage + information completeness within discovered dimensions, and separates the dimension-discovery problem (D_t->hat-D_t) from the state-extraction problem (I_t(hat-D_t)->K_t).

notations: take the distinction, refuse the ontology
note: S1-F024's consolidated, continuously-updated register of what each externally-read book/source contributes to the KnowledgeOS kernel research and its corpus disposition; the uniform pattern across nine (then fourteen) sources is 'take the distinction, refuse the ontology' -- no source proposes an adopted Kernel member, several explicitly forbid one. Distinct from individual per-book extraction documents: this is the meta-register tracking them collectively, one artifact updated per source rather than duplicated per book.

notations: Part I Perspective / Part II History / Part III The Big Three / Part IV The Contemporary Scene
note: S0705: Stewart Shapiro's 'Thinking About Mathematics: The Philosophy of Mathematics' (Oxford, 2000), a 321-page scanned-image PDF with no extractable text layer, present in the brainstorming corpus as an uploaded reference work. Structured in four parts: I Perspective (ch1-2, overview of the field and its central questions), II History (ch3 Plato & Aristotle, ch4 Kant & Mill), III The Big Three (ch5 Logicism, ch6 Formalism, ch7 Intuitionism), IV The Contemporary Scene (ch8 realism/Platonism about mathematical objects, ch9 anti-realist/nominalist views, ch10 Structuralism -- the author's own position). No companion KnowledgeOS extraction document for this book exists in this batch.

notations: dimensions -> observations -> determinations -> epistemic qualification -> knowledge
factivity, safety, recognitional ability, testimony, entitlement
aliases: What additional conditions make a determination Knowledge
note: S0707's review of an uploaded epistemology research summary (covering Williamson-style factivity, Pritchard's anti-luck/safety account, Millar's recognitional abilities, testimony, and Haddock's entitlement-vs-justification) against the ongoing dimension/state/determination model: argues a correct determination is not automatically Knowledge, and that additional epistemic-qualification conditions (factivity, safety, recognitional ability, testimony, entitlement) must be investigated before a determination is called Knowledge. Distinct from determination-as-mathematical-object (which is about formalizing the determination operation itself) -- this concerns what ADDITIONAL conditions beyond a correct determination are needed to call something Knowledge.

S0708's application of Berger & Luckmann's The Social Construction of Reality to the KnowledgeOS model: separates three questions (what is the state / what do we epistemically know about it / what does an organization socially accept as knowledge about it), introduces the social/institutional legitimation layer (objectivation, legitimation, institutionalization, distribution, maintenance, internalization), warns against reification (treating an institutional determination as a decontextualized 'thing' once its evidence/reasoning/conflict/time are forgotten), and proposes three dimension categories D^state/D^epistemic/D^social as a research hypothesis. Distinct from epistemic-qualification-conditions (S0707, which is about individual epistemic conditions for knowledge) -- this is about organizational/social legitimation of knowledge.

S0710's proposed extraction architecture: a semantic parser (not a tokenizer or embedding pipeline) that turns a sentence into semantic tokens T=(Entity,Dimension,Value,Relation,Context,Time,Source,EpistemicStatus), distinguishes directly-observed values from relationships from derived determinations (which require an explicit rule), includes a Dimension Resolver that disambiguates which canonical dimension a surface expression refers to using context, and explicitly rejects a naive Document->Chunk->Embedding->Vector->Knowledge pipeline in favor of Document->Sentence->Lexical->Syntax->Semantic Parsing->Candidate Dimensions->Dimension-Value Binding->Relationship Extraction->Evidence/Provenance->Epistemic Qualification->State Reconstruction->Reasoning/Recalculation->Knowledge State. Refines the 'smallest unit of knowledge' hypothesis to a semantically resolved assertion about a dimension plus its minimum preserving context, not a sentence or token.

notations: Is KnowledgeOS modeling reality or appearance?
aliases: Zero Lens Analysis of Ashtavakra Gita
note: S0717's own Zero-lens application to the Ashtavakra Gita (Advaita Vedanta text): maps Sat/Mithya/Asat onto the corpus's Zero categories, argues the universe/knowledge/knower are all mithya (appearance, not independently real) and only consciousness/Self is real, explicitly concludes it establishes no formal knowledge-state model or epistemology, and poses the challenge question 'is KnowledgeOS modeling reality or appearance?' with the implication that KnowledgeOS's premise of a 'state to be known' may itself be mithya. This is the primary source document that S0715 later reads, engages with, and explicitly refuses to adopt as an architectural conclusion (extracting only the anti-reification lens).
